A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM experiments on fictional and existing concepts, prototype ratings, patient recovery estimates, and robustness checks, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and reports revised sensitivity results in Figure 7. The separately attributed human studies are not needed to establish this assessment.

M1.justification: The descriptive/prescriptive framework and procedures for eliciting samples, averages, ideals, and prototype ratings are retained. Expanded reasoning-model context and revised experimental documentation do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The fictional-concept studies, existing-concept coverage, medical case study, prototype exemplars, and human-comparison tasks are retained. The concept list moves from Appendix Q to R; the new Appendix J documents an existing human comparison.

E2.justification: The evaluated model rows in Tables 2 and 15, other-model prototype comparisons, and human reference comparisons are unchanged. Newly discussed reasoning models, including o3 and DeepSeek-R1, are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Figure 7 changes the displayed ideal-value sweeps from eight to ten settings per panel and changes their ranges, although Section 4.1 still describes eight settings. Appendix I also revises the reported Experiment 4.1 prompts to omit health-benefit/risk framing, retaining the old wording in Appendix J for human comparison. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G revises the existing sensitivity analysis of sampling across statistical means and prescriptive ideals through the expanded and updated Figure 7. The other prompt-robustness, critique, prototype, and medical-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 7 replaces small scatter points around aggregate estimates with vertical error bars. The bars are not defined as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals. Reported repetition counts and statistical testing procedures elsewhere remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 7 replaces or extends plotted results and changes its correlations: for example, the first panel changes from 0.71 to 0.67 and the fourth from 0.92 to 0.57. Its settings also differ, preventing a same-setting performance interpretation. Tabulated results and the human-comparison correlations of -0.02 and 0.33 are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds mathematical reasoning about the degenerate case A(C)=I(C), declaring both deviation measures undefined. This introduces an error: Equation 1 gives unnormalized alpha equal to zero; only normalized alpha is undefined. The equations themselves and the remaining mathematical framework are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about descriptive and prescriptive influences, biased prototype ratings, possible human-value mismatch, and downstream risks remain. The rewritten prototype contribution emphasizes a finding already stated in v3's abstract and Section 5.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 6 and Appendix E reinterpret human correlations as agreement in deviation magnitude rather than overall value-system alignment, removing the inference from alpha's sign to conflicting values. v4 also qualifies the nonsignificant control result, adds optimism-bias and moral-absolutism hypotheses, and explicitly limits mechanistic interpretations.

D1.justification: v4 distinguishes complete grade-only prompts for Experiment 4.1 in Appendix I from the health-framed human-comparison prompts in Appendix J. The latter reproduce v3's Appendix I prompts, so the gain is clearer experimental attribution and specification. Compute and API disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds references to DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI reasoning models, and Li et al.'s 2025 reasoning-model survey to contextualize System-1 and System-2 behavior. Most other bibliographic revisions update retained works to publication versions rather than adding distinct research.

P1.justification: The title specifies response sampling, and the introduction, theory preface, and human-comparison discussion receive localized rewriting and expansion. Acknowledgements and a separate prompt appendix are added, while the overall narrative sequence and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 7 is redrawn with error bars, fuller axis labels and ticks, different styling, and removal of panel-specific mean titles. Figure 3 is enlarged from a wrapped inset, and its caption and Table 2's caption are expanded. Most other figures and tables retain their presentation apart from reflow and relocation.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the interpretation of human correlations and clarifies which prompts belong to each experiment. However, Figure 7 introduces unexplained changes to settings and results, undefined error bars, and a mismatch with the retained eight-setting description; Section 3.2 also introduces an incorrect mathematical statement. These competing changes leave the net effect on clarity and scientific reliability uncertain.
